source.title: Blender References Not Working | How To Set Up References Tutorial
source.creator: 3DTudor

analysis.study_scope: Analysis of reference image import failures in perspective view versus correct orthographic alignment and cross-reference setup from 00:24 to 02:04.

episodes.problem: Imported reference image aligns unpredictably to perspective viewport angle.
episodes.observed_fact: Adding a reference image while in perspective view aligns the plane to the tilted viewport angle.
episodes.instructor_claim: Importing references in perspective mode places them off-axis, hindering precise alignment.
episodes.interpretation: Blender aligns imported reference planes perpendicular to the active viewport camera angle when not locked to an orthographic view.
episodes.hypothesis: Perspective view imports cause axis misalignment.
episodes.reference_evidence: Reference image plane appears rotated at an arbitrary angle relative to global axes.
episodes.modeling_decision: Demonstrate perspective import failure to highlight orthographic requirements.
episodes.visible_action: Presses Shift+A, selects Image -> Reference, loads image, rotates viewport around cube.
episodes.spoken_reason: Show failure mode of importing reference images in perspective view.
episodes.failure: Reference image plane is angled arbitrarily, preventing accurate orthographic modeling.
episodes.correction: Delete misaligned reference plane and switch to orthographic view.
episodes.alternatives: Manually reset rotation values in Transform panel.
episodes.transferable_principle: Always switch to a locked orthographic view before importing reference images.

episodes.problem: Need reference image aligned precisely along global axes.
episodes.observed_fact: Switching to Front Orthographic view before importing aligns reference flat along front axis.
episodes.instructor_claim: Pressing Numpad 1 puts viewport in front view so reference aligns perfectly.
episodes.interpretation: Orthographic views constrain new reference plane orientation flat to the view axis.
episodes.hypothesis: Front orthographic import zeros out tilt rotation axes automatically.
episodes.reference_evidence: Reference image plane aligns parallel to XZ plane.
episodes.modeling_decision: Import reference image while locked in Front Orthographic view.
episodes.visible_action: Deletes old reference, presses Numpad 1, presses Shift+A -> Image -> Reference to reload image.
episodes.spoken_reason: Ensure image plane aligns perfectly for front modeling.
episodes.topology_surface_effect: Plane created flat facing front orthographic view.
episodes.transferable_principle: Import reference images from standard orthographic views to guarantee exact axis alignment.

episodes.problem: Single reference plane lacks multi-angle view coverage.
episodes.observed_fact: Duplicating reference plane and rotating 90 degrees on Z creates cross-reference layout.
episodes.instructor_claim: Duplicating and rotating reference 90 degrees allows viewing geometry from all sides, especially in wireframe mode.
episodes.interpretation: Crossed orthographic planes paired with wireframe display allow continuous multi-axis modeling reference.
episodes.hypothesis: Wireframe view combined with crossed planes prevents geometry from obscuring reference details.
episodes.reference_evidence: Two orthographic reference planes intersect at 90 degrees around center geometry.
episodes.modeling_decision: Duplicate front plane, rotate 90 degrees on Z axis, add cube, and switch to wireframe mode.
episodes.visible_action: Presses Shift+D, Enter, R Z 90. Adds cube, scales it, presses Z -> Wireframe.
episodes.spoken_reason: Provide full multi-side reference coverage for modeling.
episodes.topology_surface_effect: Intersecting reference planes surround central model volume.
episodes.alternatives: Use multi-viewport setup with separate orthographic images.
episodes.transferable_principle: Crossed orthographic reference planes combined with wireframe view enable accurate multi-axis mesh alignment.

rejected_sections: 00:50 - 01:06: Channel logo sequence and video introduction
limitations: Analysis restricted strictly to interval 00:24 to 02:04.
